fields.evidence: Creator bg3.exe+0x3E81900 allocates 0x40 bytes and zeroes the HashMap members; destructor bg3.exe+0x5C4870 frees the value buffer at +0x30 without element destructor and the key part (bg3.exe+0x582AD0). macOS component destructor: frees +0x30, then ls::HashTable<ls::ID<EntityHandleTraits>, ls::ClusterHashTableOps>::~HashTable(this) - entity-handle keys. Windows ClusterLoadHelper<ClusterPhysicsLoaderSystem::LoadOps> code bg3.exe+0x3E7BA90 gets the singleton through bg3.exe+0x3E7DCA0 (storage index DAT_1463d4084), inserts the 8-byte entity handles of each cluster's content key array (stride 8) with bg3.exe+0x1D3C100 / bg3.exe+0x135D7A0 and stores an 8-byte value per key ('*(undefined8 *)(*(map + 0x30) + idx * 8) = *cluster'): content entity -> owning cluster entity. Same shape as ls::ClusterVisibilityRegisterySingletonComponent (layouts\alive). Note: the game hashes keys with ClusterHashTableOps (key % bucket count). Live: up to 0xD653 keys.

summary: Client streaming singleton: a large hash map (tens of thousands of entries) used by the cluster physics loader (ls::ClusterPhysicsLoaderSystem); lives from game start.
open_questions: The name follows the visual twin's layout (ClusterOfContent), not a game member name.
